_about: Anti-aircraft battery: the strike's defence (Alex's decision strike-plan, 2026-10-10: two batteries whose flak uses the cone system aimed upward, strong in the low and medium bands and weak in the high one; and his decision low-band-flak, 2026-10-10: flak more dangerous in the LOW band). A STATIC unit (mobility 'static'): it never moves, turns or plans. TWO weapons, both all-around cones aimed UP with flexible-gun tracking, each rolling for itself: FLAK (heavy: long reach, 900 m effective, strong in the low and medium bands, weak in the high one) and LIGHT_FLAK (added by Track F: short reach, 320 m effective, so it covers the low band near the battery and does not reach the medium band at all). Its band is the surface; it goes down with the fate 'destroyed' at 0 health, so bombs can silence it. EVERY NUMBER IS PROPOSED (the heavy flak by Track S2, the light flak by Track F, 2026-10-10); the bands come out as Alex asked from the cones' lowest angle (2 degrees: nothing is out of the cone for being low) and the two effective ranges (heavy 900 m, reach 1,080 m with the common 20 percent overshoot, just under the high band's height of 1,000 m; light 320 m, reach 384 m, under the 397 m of a plane right over the guns in the medium band). A plane flying straight over ONE battery takes, in expected pips (scripts/test_support/strike_tuning.gd, table A, the battery's rolls only, light guns included): bomber low 4.8 (heavy 2.8 + light 2.0), medium 2.7, high 0.35; light fighter low 3.9 (2.3 + 1.6), medium 2.2, high 0.3; passing 300 m to one side the bomber takes 3.6 at low (2.7 + 0.9) and 2.6 at medium. BEFORE THE LIGHT GUNS low and medium were the same, 2.8 and 2.7 for the bomber (the 3.4 once printed for the low bomber counted its own turret fire at the battery as well). Two batteries on a bomber's bomb run at the tower (table C, 300 seeds, aligned track): the bomber loses about half its 8 pips by the verdict at medium (3.5, shot down 8 percent) and 3.9 at low (shot down 5 percent; 3.1 and 0 percent with the heavy flak alone), 0.2 at high. In the real Strike scenario (the batteries 234 and 271 m off the bomber's line) the scripted bomber (strike_play.gd, 40 seeds, the three planes low) loses 4.4 pips of 8 with the light guns, 2.3 without, 2.1 at medium, and wins every run. A MODEST step by Alex's own rule (2026-10-10: the playtest is not calibrated, the scenario favours the attackers): the order is low worse than medium worse than high, not a death zone; the dial is light_flak's base_hit_chance. Record shape: data/units/_schema.json.
name: Anti-aircraft battery

size_m._reason: a gun pit, a sandbag ring and two or three guns seen from above

actions_per_turn._reason: a static unit has nothing to plan: one step a turn that stands still

health._reason: a bomb's direct hit is 3 pips and a near miss 2 or 1 (data/sim/bombs.json): a battery goes down to two near hits or a direct hit and a graze, so the bomber can silence one on its way in at the price of bombs the tower needs

sight_range_m._reason: spotters with the guns: sees about as far as a fighter's 800 m, a little less; the enemy AI counts what its units see (scripts/sim/ai_sense.gd), including its static units, so this is how far a battery warns the patrol

turn_bleed_exponent._reason: static: never turns (the exponent is unused; it must be a number)

altitude_bands._reason: it stands on the ground: the surface band (data/sim/altitude.json)

hardpoints._reason: Track S2: the guns' muzzles about six metres above the ground, at the battery's centre; the height is part of the cone's geometry (a plane at 120 m is 114 m above the muzzle)

mount_deg._reason: Track S2: the cone is all around (half_across 180), so the mount does not matter; 0 is the battery's heading

half_across_deg._reason: Track S2: all around. 180 means the azimuth is not part of the cone test (combat.gd): flak fires at anything above it, whichever way the battery faces

elevation_deg._reason: Track S2: Alex's accepted proposal, flak on upward cones. The cone is centred 46 degrees above the horizon

half_height_deg._reason: Track S2: from 2 degrees above the horizon to straight up (90). 2 and not 10: a first try with a 10 degree floor left the low band (120 m) out of the cone beyond 680 m of ground distance and made it the LEAST dangerous band (measured at a base chance of 0.05: 1.8 pips a pass against the medium band's 1.9); with a 2 degree floor the cone's edge is the weapon's range (892 m at 120 m) and the low band comes out strongest (3.4 pips a pass against the medium band's 2.7)

effective_range_m._reason: Track S2: strong in the low and medium bands, weak in the high one (Alex's accepted proposal). 900 m effective, 1,080 m reach with the common range_overshoot (data/sim/combat.json): the low band is inside the effective range out to 892 m of ground distance, the medium band out to 806 m; a plane overhead in the high band (1,000 m) is in the fringe at 42 percent of the odds, 200 m to one side at 26 percent, 400 m to one side at nothing

base_hit_chance._reason: Track S2: a battery makes 0.14 hits a second on a plane in the cone before the other factors (two rolls a second at 0.07). Tuned in the tuning tables: at 0.05 a bomber lost 2.8 pips of 8 to two batteries before its bombs landed from low and 3.2 from medium and was never shot down from low, which is not 'strong'; at 0.07 it loses 3.7 and 4.0 and is shot down 1 and 11 percent of the time (aligned runs)

rim_odds_factor._reason: Track S2: flat, as the other flexible guns and turrets: a gun crew aims within the arc

falloff_exponent._reason: Track S2: no effect while the factor is flat (rim_odds_factor 1)

tracking_dps._reason: Track S2: flexible-gun tracking (Alex's accepted proposal), 20 deg/s like the bomber's nose gun and the heavy fighter's rear gunner. A bomber overhead at 400 m crosses the line of sight at about 12 deg/s (factor 0.73); at 120 m at about 40 deg/s (0.2): flak cannot swing fast enough for a plane right overhead at low height, so the low band is most dangerous on the approach and the way out. Doubling it to 40 changed a pass over a battery by under 10 percent, so it is not the lever

damage_pips._reason: Track S2: a burst is one pip, like a machine gun's hit; a bomber's 8 pips and a light fighter's 3 are weighed against it

rolls_per_second._reason: Track S2: the same burst rate as every machine gun in the game

hardpoints._reason: Track F (2026-10-10): the light guns' muzzles about three metres above the ground at the battery's centre (the heavy flak's are six): smaller guns on lower mounts. A plane at 120 m is 117 m above them, one at 400 m 397 m

mount_deg._reason: Track F: the cone is all around (half_across 180), so the mount does not matter; 0 is the battery's heading, as for the heavy flak

half_across_deg._reason: Track F: all around, like the heavy flak: the azimuth is not part of the cone test (combat.gd), the guns fire at anything above them whichever way the battery faces

elevation_deg._reason: Track F: the heavy flak's cone, so the two weapons agree on what is above the battery: centred 46 degrees above the horizon

half_height_deg._reason: Track F: from 2 degrees above the horizon to straight up, as the heavy flak's (its reason has the 10-degree floor that made the low band the LEAST dangerous): the cone's edge is the range, nothing is out of it for being low

effective_range_m._reason: Track F, the low-band lever (Alex's decision low-band-flak, 2026-10-10: make flak more dangerous in the low band; lever (a), a second weapon, data only). SHORT, so it reaches the low band (120 m) near the battery and not the medium band (400 m): reach 384 m with the common 20 percent overshoot, under the 397 m of a plane flying right over the guns at medium, so the medium band is out of its reach everywhere (table A, light part: 0.00 in every medium and high row). At low it covers a ring of about 300 m round the battery at full odds (298 m of ground distance at 120 m) and out to 366 m in the fringe. A plane flying straight over ONE battery (strike_tuning.gd table A, expected pips, heavy flak alone -> with the light guns): bomber low 2.80 -> 4.76 over it, 2.73 -> 3.59 passing 300 m aside, 2.36 -> 2.36 at 600 m; light fighter low 2.32 -> 3.94, 2.24 -> 2.96, 1.95 -> 1.95; medium (2.68 / 2.57 / 2.08 bomber, 2.20 / 2.12 / 1.73 fighter) and high (0.35 and 0.29 over it) unchanged. Brittle at the ring's edge by nature, a short gun's effect depends on how close the track passes (table C, batteries 300 m off the line: the aligned track gains 0.8 pips, one 40 m off, 340 m from one battery, 0.2; the real strike's batteries stand 234 and 271 m off the bomber's line and the bomber gains 2.1)

base_hit_chance._reason: Track F: the heavy flak's own per-roll chance (0.07) at twice its roll rate, so 0.28 hits a second on a plane in range before the other factors (the heavy flak's 0.14). A MODEST step on purpose (Alex 2026-10-10: the playtest is not calibrated and the scenario favours the attackers, so the aim is the ORDER, low clearly worse than medium, not a hard low band). The dial, with the bomber's pips lost of 8 (the heavy flak alone / this / 0.10 / 0.14; medium for comparison, which no value here changes): table A, one battery, straight over at low: 2.80 / 4.76 / 5.61 / 6.73 (medium 2.68); table C, two batteries 300 m off, aligned track, 300 seeds, pips lost (shot down): 3.10 (0%) / 3.93 (5%) / 4.32 (7%) / 4.77 (11%) (medium 3.53, 8%); the real Strike scenario played by the scripted bomber (strike_play.gd, 40 seeds, all three planes low): 2.33 / 4.38 / 5.28 / 6.35, won 40 of 40 at every value (medium 2.15). 0.07 doubles the bomber's losses in the real scenario and keeps the win; 0.14 would put its mean at 6.4 of 8 pips there, a death zone, which is why it is not used

rim_odds_factor._reason: Track F: flat, as the heavy flak and every flexible gun: a gun crew aims within the arc

falloff_exponent._reason: Track F: no effect while the factor is flat (rim_odds_factor 1)

tracking_dps._reason: Track F: fast tracking, it is a light gun: three times the heavy flak's 20 deg/s. A plane right over the guns at low height crosses the line of sight at 43 to 52 deg/s (bomber, light fighter): factor 0.66 for the bomber where the heavy flak's 20 gives 0.18. Re-check that raising the HEAVY flak's tracking_dps alone is not the lever (table A, expected pips, bomber over the battery at 20 -> 60 deg/s): low 2.80 -> 3.12 (+11%), medium 2.68 -> 2.95 (+10%), high 0.35 -> 0.36; at 120 deg/s 3.21 and 2.98. It lifts low and medium together, so it cannot make low more dangerous than medium. Nor does this value shape the light guns' pass: 60 -> 40 takes about 9 percent off their part

damage_pips._reason: Track F: one pip a hit like every other gun; the light guns hurt by volume (four rolls a second), not by weight of shell. A bomber's 8 pips and a light fighter's 3 are weighed against it

rolls_per_second._reason: Track F: a roll every tick (data/sim/combat.json tick_seconds 0.25, the finest the sim resolves), twice a machine gun's two rolls a second: light guns are fast guns. Rolls draw one flak burst each on the effects layer (combat_feed.gd), so this also doubles the bursts a battery shows over a low plane, a rough edge of the effects, not of the numbers
